title: 6 relatives on a fishing trip were killed after their plane crashed near Mississippi’s Horn Island | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

Six relatives from two families who were on a fishing trip together died when a small plane carrying them crashed Tuesday nearMississippi’s Horn Island, according to their families.

A joint statement from their families identified them as Brent Stokes, 50, and his son, Hunter Stokes, 16; Arlyn Knox, 43; her husband, Michael Knox, 43; and the couple’s sons, Charles Holden Knox, 12, and Truett Knox, 10. Brent Stokes and Arlyn Knox were siblings.

Authorities have not publicly identified those on board. The US Coast Guard initially said four adults and two boys believed to be between 8 and 10 years old were aboard the plane.

The plane, a Cessna Centurion 210 aircraft, was carrying the families who were on a trip to celebrate the start of the holiday season, before it crashed Tuesday afternoon, their relatives said.

Brent Stokes was piloting the plane, and they were heading home to Fort Myers, Florida, to join the rest of their family for the Thanksgiving holiday, according to their families.

“They died doing what they loved,” the family statement said. “In the middle of our grief, we are holding on to that, and to how much love they gave us and how much love surrounds us now. We will carry them with us always.”

The Coast Guard on Tuesday received a call around 3:45 p.m. after the FAA lost communication with the aircraft, a spokesperson for the US Coast Guard Mobile told CNN earlier in the day.

Flight tracking data showed the Cessna 210 flying from New Orleans to Fort Myers.

About 30 minutes after takeoff, while it was at about 8,800 feet in the air, just south of Pascagoula, Mississippi, the plane suddenly plunged toward the water, according to the website Flightradar24. The aircraft was diving at 18,000 feet a minute, more than 200 miles per hour, in the final seconds before the tracking data stopped at around 3:30 p.m.

The search for the six people on board, which lasted about four hours, concluded “when divers from the Mississippi Department of Marine Resources (MDMR) located the remains of all six individuals within the fuselage of the aircraft,” the US Coast Guard said in anews release.

“This is a heartbreaking outcome, and our deepest sympathies are with the families and loved ones who are facing an unimaginable loss,” said Cmdr. Trevor Blount, the Coast Guard Sector Mobile search and rescue mission coordinator.

“While this is not the outcome any of us had hoped for, we are grateful for the strong interagency coordination that enabled us to swiftly locate those aboard the aircraft and provide closure to their families,” he added.

Crews searching the scene had earlier found three life jackets, a life raft and the cabin of the aircraft, a Coast Guard spokesperson said.

The National Transportation Safety Board is leading the investigation into the crash, according to the Federal Aviation Administration, which will also be assisting in the probe.

Horn Island is a remote, undeveloped island about 12 nautical miles from Biloxi, Mississippi, that is only accessible by private boat. The journey from nearby Biloxi, Ocean Springs, or Pascagoula takes about 30 minutes to an hour.

The island is part of the Gulf Islands National Seashore, a national park that includes a dozen islands stretching 160 miles across Mississippi and Florida.

Horn Island is about 10 miles long and only about a mile wide. It is a popular summer destination for state residents.

This story has been updated with additional information.

CNN’s Alisha Ebrahimji contributed to this report.

CNN’s Alisha Ebrahimji contributed to this report.
